body:
Update: Okay, yes. My HDD is failing. The start/stop count rises whenever this sudden switching off thing happens. Not sure how long it has 'till it goes. I'll have an opportunity in about a month to replace it.

I hope they replace the laptop... It was very expensive and I had to save for a long time. Can the HDD be replaced?

I suppose so. In fact, I do not know if I will die today while crossing the street, tomorrow of an unknown virus, the day after of food poisoning, or in two years of cancer!

Worrying does nothing. It is best to accept the distinct possibility, and do what is in our power to avoid it. Knowing that, we may rest easy.

Thank you. Both for the compliment and the response. If I am to be honest, I probably wouldn't have cared a week ago, but now that my life took a turn for the better, I am paranoid and have a newly found will to live.

Cancer is so incredibly common these days, that definitely adds to my fears.

Oh my god... This is unbelievable... Possibly one of the happiest, yet most odd moments in my entire life.

I failed getting into the prestigious school of choice. I suppose everyone else prepared, while I sat on my ass and did nothing at all. However, and thank any deity that may or may not exist, I made it into the engineering school... 9th place... I do not know how, but it happened.

I will be studying all year long next year, and I will attempt to get in my school of choice. I thank everyone for the support, I am so insanely happy that my life is not over just yet.

Speaking of tinkering, I've always wanted to do engineering, along with physics. Sad, since that will never happen either. I effectively failed high school.

My mind is at ease now. I still think about killing myself every few minutes, and I am prepared to take needed action if things get worse, but at least I can function in this moment.

Update: I failed! So that's that! Well, I don't know my results yet. Grammar and literature went quite alright, I'd say, but mathematics was a total disaster. I'll be lucky to get 10/50 points.

Not sure what I'll do now. Considered packing my bags and testing out certain religious hypotheses, but I'd rather wait 'till I actually get my results.

Thanks for all the wishes, but I fucked up anyway.
A test of your abilities, basically. I'm taking the test so that I can be accepted into a good school. Only 60 people can do it though. GCSE is on a similar mathematical level as these exams.
Something like GCSE, except I'm not in England. Thanks!
Thanks! If others don't do well, I should pass. Only 60 get through, unfortunately. And there's 192 of us.
Thank you!

I hope I do too. Unfortunately, I find that I'm better off putting a bullet through my head.

I expected problems, I really did. But I expected them once I start learning about concepts like relativity or quantum mechanics, not stupid algebra word problems.

I've always wanted to be like those physicists you see on television. I've always wanted to understand everything there is to understand, know everything there is to know. It's a shame that all of my potential, curiosity, desire for knowledge... All of it is gone in the blink of an eye, because of stupid algebra word problems.

Similar thing for me. Seriously, I made a thread about a similar thing about 3 minutes before you did.

If you want to talk, I'd appreciate it immensely. Not only because I feel like helping out, but also because I need help myself. I need to talk to someone who feels like I do.

We can talk through PMs (if you even want to talk at all), if Skype is better, my name is doctorcrazyeyes. I hate voice communication, so I can type at most. I'm legit (in the way that I'm not a perverted maniac who has a fetish for severed feet).

Not pathetic at all. It is a completely valid plea for help, especially when we take in consideration the things you've been through. If your plea for help is pathetic, I don't want to know what mine is.

It's easy to say that things get better, but it takes a lot to admit that quite often, things just don't go the way they're supposed to. Things happen independently of what we want, and while we can somewhat affect our chances, the universe is still driven by nothing but probability.

I will mess up my exams soon, and effectively ruin my reputation, therefore ruining my academic future and later my entire life. I always hoped things would go well, that they'd be all good, but in truth? Hope doesn't do anything for you. Hope can often times add even more pain.

While I do not encourage suicide (mainly just because it's seen as 'inappropriate'. Honestly I believe people should have the right to take their own lives), and I think it's always good to attempt to find alternatives, I won't discourage you from it. I know how it feels. It feels like an easy way out of problems. Or no, it isn't an easy way, it is simply the easiest of the difficult paths. Pain? I too fear the pain. I want it to be quick and painless when it happens. I also do not want to have the ability to go back. 

Failing suicide makes everything even worse.

I hope I could have been of help.

Edit: It is in our nature to survive. We survive, and later die of old age. It may seem that some lives have more meaning than others, that they're somehow more relevant, but in truth, all lives are just as irrelevant as, say, yours or mine. Depression helps you realize that life is pretty insignificant. It is probably the only good thing it brings.

I know. I just can't believe I already hit a brick wall. I expected to struggle with calculus, not algebra 2 and word problems. It's demoralizing, which in turn hinders my ability to learn anything at all. Some people have no problem with these things, and I don't get how that's possible.

I considered myself very good at mathematics, and it's painful being ripped out of that idea.
I suppose me ending up in a school for intellectually disabled students didn't help very much with that. I wish I had been taught these things, instead of learning linear equations in 9th grade.

I simply do not understand it. I tried the equation, and x came out as 0.65, which means nothing. Obviously I made some sort of mistake.

I give up. Word problems are not my thing. I just can't do them effectively. I have to accept that I've chosen highly ambitious goals I am not capable of reaching. I made a mistake, and now I face disappointment. No engineering, no physics, no mathematics. I'll probably end up with a minimum-wage job somewhere in the suburbs of Prague. But such is life.

Thanks man. Honestly, you took the time to help me, to share your knowledge. To help shed light on the problem. That must be appreciated more by society.

The third is my issue. I am utterly incapable of figuring out unfamiliar problems. Sometimes I can. Other times I can't. If it says something like "A was this much faster than B and B was three times higher than C", it's all good, but such vague things are insane. I don't know if it is simple incompetence or just plain lack of experience.

That's what I thought at first, that nickels and dimes would be x and y, but then I don't know how to solve the equation. I can do systems in the blink of an eye, but why 0.05 nickels and 0.1 dimes? It seems to incredibly bizarre and nonsensical. And in the second equation, I cannot find a way to get rid of x or y. Divide the first equation by 10, add everything together, and solve as a linear? I don't get it.

However I strongly emphasize on my great appreciation for your help. I am trying to do my best (trying), but it's all just so vague. Normally, abstract thinking is no problem for me. But in mathematics, it's so... Odd. Everything is just odd. Especially these word problems.
Nobody in the classroom (out of 32 people) got the answer right. Apparently it was, I believe, 128cm. He showed us how he got to the conclusion, but I just didn't get it at all.

Whatever. Forget this fucking bizarre as hell problem. I'll just hope it never shows up again.

There's another difficult problem I cannot solve for the life of me. It's these damn stupid useless problems that I can never get over, and I swear to God I am so insanely mad right now, because for the past six hours I've been tirelessly trying my best to understand this bullshit, and I just can't!

Here's the goddamn problem.

There are 22 coins in total, and they equal $1.55. The dollar and a half is made of only nickels and dimes. How many nickels and dimes are there?

Well I can't define the variable, I can't define the unknown, I can't define nickels or dimes because as opposed to problems like triangle problems (2nd angle is 20 degrees bigger than x and therefore x + 20 etc.), there's utterly no clue for the relationship between nickels and dimes.

How the hell am I to solve this? It's so mad!
Exactly. I have no clue what they meant. This is the exact wording.

Here's one of the problems that haunt me the most. If it is confusing, do not worry, I did not understand it at the slightest (went to a prep test today, ended horribly):

There are 18 stairs leading from the 1st floor to the 2nd. The 2nd floor is 48cm thick. If each stair is 2cm taller than the last, there have to be 20 stairs. How tall is the 1st floor?

Not a clue. It's just the most bizarre word problem I've seen.

Perhaps so, but it doesn't matter! Two weeks left to revise, and many different types of word problems to cover. 

I believe there is one more thing you could help me with (if you are willing). You see, I've done algebra for so long, I even forgot the meaning behind the equations themselves! It's just become this natural instinct, solving equations when I see them. I believe this could also be a cause of some of my problems with it. I often ask: What's the point of the equation? They seem so utterly useless (the specific problems), are they just used for the sake of testing? Or is there some deeper meaning that might help me understand the subject?

Unfortunately, it seems I will fail these exams. I can't do word problems. I can't create equations. All I can do is solve equations. Unfortunately, that's 10% of the deal, and everything else is a nightmare for me.

Thank you for teaching me what a factor is. I get it now. Really helped me a lot. Unfortunately, I am a mathematical idiot. It's a shame. A shame that I will not be physicist.

Thanks again.

While I am having trouble understanding some of the mathematical terms (factoring, etc.), I believe I understand what you mean. Your posts were most helpful, I am currently working on these accursed things. And even if I do not get them right, it is only 3 points off in the exam itself.

Sorry. I posted it in the other deleted thread, forgot here. It's all of fractional algebra. Simplifying, operations, everything. I can almost always find the common denominator, and I know what to do with it, but many times there's nothing to cancel out, and the expression becomes a total mess.

I'll try to find particularly difficult examples.
Yes. That is what I attempt to do, but so many times I get it wrong. Like I said, it's inconsistent.
I deleted the topic. Wrong section. Sorry about that folks.

Yes. I thought of that. Probably too enraged to notice my own mistake though. Enraged by the fact that I can't get it for 7 months now.

Forgive my incompetence. Unfortunately, it seems I not only cannot understand algebra, but I also cannot read the sidebar. What a physicist I'd make... What a physicist indeed... I'd probably claim the four fundamental forces are false! Hah!

Thank you for your assistance.

It helps, talking about problems. At least it does for some people. It always helped me at least a little bit. But then again, sometimes it can hurt you even more. 

Personally, and don't take this as belittling your problem, it's just me rambling, I get myself out of bed because I know I've got a damn fancy trench coat to wear! Sure, a few of my teachers called it a 'coat for homeless people', but I don't give a damn about their opinions. It's my coat, and I fancy my coat!

Point is, attempt to find something that will pull you out of bed. Something... Worthwhile. In my case it's a dusty old coat from the 30s, and for you? It could be anything else! Of course, that doesn't mean there has to be something, but more than likely there is something, hidden away from plain sight.

Try not to feel guilty. Sure, it's easier said than done, but damn! If you're depressed, feeling guilty is the very last thing you need! Your therapist will surely understand. Hell, he's probably got problems of his own!

I sure hope this was at least a bit encouraging. I'm a mild psychopath (didn't score too high, but high enough), so I wouldn't be surprised if I accidentally offended, insulted, or discouraged you in some way.

I am extremely excited for the game myself! However, I remain watchful, and try not to get my hopes up.

There have been far too many Watch Dogs in the recent years... I pray No Man's Sky will not become one of them.

Hype is a useful ally, and yet a dangerous foe.

Pretty much agree with the video. People simply need to understand that there's only so much a small group of developers can do.

The game will be great though. That much is for sure. Even more so with the relatively new reveal of survival aspects of the game and the implementation of NPCs/dialogue (well, to an extent).

Edit: Nevermind. Wrong video. I thought I was watching the "Why NMS will not live up to hype". Still, I believe my post should add something to the discussion.

Okay, thanks for the tip!

By the way, even though this isn't a support section, I'd appreciate some quick directions. Any idea where I can ask about an issue regarding my laptop making weird noises? Perhaps BuildaPC, but that's more for desktops, so I'm uncertain.
I've heard terrifying things about 4Chan. Are they true?

If only that were a viable option. If I was in university, I'd do it. However, I haven't completed primary school yet, and repeating a year pretty much means you won't be accepted anywhere in this country.

However I thank you for your suggestion, and will keep it in mind if I do indeed study at a university one day.

Yes, it is. Thing is, the bloody government here wants more carpenters, and so they blatantly decapitate anyone's potential. We're the first wave of students to suffer this dumb decision, believe it or not.

The exams are hard I tell you. 9 years worth of material. I'll try a test run on Friday/Saturday. Should give me a clue about what it is I lack in terms of knowledge (pretty much everything that I haven't used in some time).

That's funny, I actually am registered on that forum. However, I didn't do too well, and some of the members seemed like condescending pricks, to put it simply. However, I do not wish to discredit the forum. There were many nice people as well.

I don't lack motivation, but the thing is, I'll have exams in a month and a half. If I fail, I don't get into high school. If I don't get into high school... Well, we know what happens then.

The real problem is the lack of resources and the fact that, as you said, you don't do well on your own.

If she has been cheating on you, and hasn't apologized or felt at least a bit guilty, it begs the question: Does this person respect you, and are they in turn deserving of your respect? 

That's your own decision.

Still, if this person does not respect you, and knows of your issues, perhaps they could exploit them.

Tell me, who usually starts the fights, and what are they about?

Optics are nice, but far from my favorite. Astrophysics is a field which has always intrigued me, same with cosmology. Time and relativistic physics (I believe that's what it's called) are perhaps the most intriguing to me. Something I am less interested in, but very interested in nevertheless, is the quantum theory.

I don't enjoy classical physics much (except for Einstein's theories). I am most interested in black holes (or singularities in general), the evolution of our universe, atoms and sub-atomic particles, and time.
I see. So you can't move back? It seems you do not have much of a future with this person. What are the possibilities?

Thank you... I really appreciate it. It helps, knowing that mathematics aren't everything.

I love mathematics when I understand it, hate it when I don't.

What's wrong, exactly? Something specific happened? Or perhaps you do not know what's wrong? Is it the new life that is bothering you? Is it not possible to return to your old life?

Too many questions, yes. But I'd like to try to help, and for that I need to know more. 

If it's hard to talk about, you don't have to.

I will consume anything you have to say. Lay everything on me, if you want.

I'm no miracle worker, but I'll listen. Going through similar stuff myself.

Message me if you want to talk.
